title: Engineering Enablement Programs
framing: How I build enablement programs, worked example: MuleSoft Days, a self-service training curriculum I designed and launched — 53+ documented participants, with continued organic use across the engineering organization years after launch. The structure below is the shape that program followed; the office-hours/coaching cadence is how I'd extend it in a formal Developer Experience role.

case_study.name: MuleSoft Days
case_study.problem: API-led architecture and MuleSoft adoption were growing faster than any one team could onboard engineers 1:1. New contributors needed a consistent, credible on-ramp that didn't depend on whoever happened to be free that week.
case_study.approach: A self-service, video-based curriculum engineers could work through at their own pace, deliberately built to reinforce the golden-path templates and reuse patterns already in place rather than teaching MuleSoft in the abstract.
case_study.outcome: 53+ documented participants at launch, with continued organic use well beyond the initial cohort — the strongest signal a self-service program actually stuck rather than fading once the launch push ended.

learning_path.title: Foundations
learning_path.description: Core concepts and vocabulary, oriented around why the platform's conventions exist, not just what they are.

learning_path.title: Golden-Path Build
learning_path.description: Build a real integration starting from the enterprise's golden-path template, reinforcing reuse over building from scratch.

learning_path.title: Patterns in Practice
learning_path.description: Common integration patterns pulled directly from production examples, not textbook cases — the same patterns a new contributor will actually run into.

learning_path.title: Production Readiness
learning_path.description: What separates a working integration from a production-ready one: testing, error handling, observability, and the review expectations engineers should anticipate.

cadence.title: Weekly office hours
cadence.description: A standing, low-friction slot for whoever's mid-module and stuck — optional, drop-in, no prep required on either side.

cadence.title: Cohort check-ins
cadence.description: A lightweight touchpoint partway through a cohort's progression, surfacing where the curriculum itself is unclear before it becomes everyone's individual problem.

cadence.title: Escalation to 1:1 coaching
cadence.description: For anyone still stuck after office hours — the exception path, not the default, so the self-service model stays the primary on-ramp rather than becoming shadow 1:1 training.

reinforcement: Golden-path template usage is directly observable (see the Golden-Path Demo section of how-it-was-built.html) — adoption isn't just self-reported.
Curriculum content stays tied to the real, current templates and patterns, not a static snapshot that drifts out of date.
Organic reuse well past the initial launch cohort is the real success signal — a program only leadership pushes stops the moment leadership stops pushing it.
